summary: Retest of the fixed-fee-slab sub-category bug (backend + frontend). Backend: 15/15 pytest checks passed, including the reported order 100137423450 / LTQRTOPS119573072 which now matches slab label 'Tops' with fixed_fee 52.0 (was 'Dresses'). Full audit over ALL 42,550 calculations (paginated via GET /api/calculations, order_type sales=27,942 + return=14,608) found 0 cases where breakdown.fixed_fee_slab.label != breakdown.sub_category; only 2 sales rows have no slab at all (no label -> not a mismatch, part of the accepted unmapped set). Recalc smoke: POST /api/calculations/run {recalculate:true} -> 200 in 5.4s, processed=42550, total_sales=42550, unmapped_count=573, fully_mapped_count=41977 (exact expected values). Frontend: login admin@fundle.ai/admin123 OK; Calculations drawer for the reported Tops order shows 'Fixed Fee Slab: Tops -> Rs 52'; verified 12 drawers across Tops/Trousers/Blazers/Coats filters - every drawer's slab label equals the row's Sub Category. Regression in drawer OK: Commission @12.00% / 700-1050, GT (Level 1) 700-1050 x 1 -> Rs 31.86/u, Return Fee (Zone National) 'Not applied' for a sale, Total Deductions Rs 214.72 / Expected Settlement Rs 608.42 computed. Masters GT=96 rows and Return Fee=12 rows confirmed via API; no 'kazo' string in the rendered DOM on Calculations or Masters pages. One NEW minor frontend defect found: the Sub-Category exact filter suffers a stale-response race (see below).

integration_issues.flow: Calculations page -> Sub-Category (exact) filter / search interplay
integration_issues.issue: No debounce or request cancellation on the sub_category filter: load() fires on every keystroke and the search field has its own 400ms debounced load(). Slower earlier responses overwrite newer ones (last-response-wins), so the grid can display rows for a different sub-category than the one shown in the filter box. Reproduced: type 'LTQR' in search, clear it, then type 'Coats' in Sub-Category -> input shows 'Coats' but all 2,543 listed rows are 'Tops'. Typing 'Tops' alone works correctly. Data correctness is unaffected (the slab invariant still holds), but the filter is misleading.

action_items: OPTIONAL (minor): debounce the Sub-Category (exact) filter in /app/frontend/src/pages/Calculations.jsx and guard load() against stale responses (AbortController or a request sequence token) so the grid always matches the active filters.
OPTIONAL (nit): clearFilters() in Calculations.jsx rebuilds the filters object without the 'order_type' key, dropping it from state shape; include order_type: "" for consistency.
critical_code_review_comments: _match_fixed_fee falls back to band-only slabs only when NO sub-category-scoped slab exists; if a sub-category has slabs but none covers the ISP the result is None (correctly flagged unmapped) rather than silently borrowing another sub-category's slab. Behaviour verified against data - good.

_match_fixed_fee keys on s['sub_category'] or s['label']; the LQ fixed-fee master (272 rows) has both fields populated and identical, so matching is unambiguous today. If a future upload sets only 'label' as a display string, matching would silently degrade - consider requiring sub_category explicitly.

rca_of_the_issue: Original RCA (fixed): _match_fixed_fee iterated all fixed-fee slabs and returned the first whose AISP band contained the ISP, ignoring sub_category, while LQ's fixed fees are per-sub-category (272 rows, many overlapping bands) - so a Tops order picked whichever sub-category's slab appeared first in the list (e.g. Dresses). Fix filters the slab pool by sub_category (case-insensitive) before the band check, with a fallback to global slabs that carry no sub_category. Verified across every persisted calculation: 0 mismatches.
